data.title: Al-Khudeir Season Brings Color to Jazan's Fields, Revitalizes Markets with Fresh Sorghum
data.content:
Jazan, November 22, 2026, SPA -- Sorghum farms across Jazan Region are witnessing renewed activity with the arrival of Al-Khudeir season, when freshly harvested sorghum meets the culinary traditions of Jazan. The season reflects the region's rich agricultural and culinary heritage and the deep connection between residents and their locally grown crops. White and red varieties of sorghum are cultivated across more than 60,000 hectares, from coastal plains to mountain villages, highlighting the crop's importance to the region's social and economic life.
    The fields take on shades of green and yellow as farmers begin harvesting sorghum heads before they fully ripen. Careful timing is essential to preserve the grains' tenderness, quality, and distinctive flavor. The season takes its name, Al-Khudeir, from the green color of the immature grains. These are carefully selected and collected for transport to homes and markets using techniques passed down through generations.
    At traditional markets, bundles of fresh sorghum heads feature prominently among seasonal produce, attracting local buyers and allowing farmers to sell their harvest directly. Prices vary according to the size and quality of the crop. The resulting commercial activity reflects its nutritional and economic value and highlights the importance of local varieties among Jazan's seasonal agricultural products.
    The traditional process known as "Al-Khabit" showcases another aspect of the region's agricultural heritage. Sorghum grains are separated from their heads by beating them with sticks. Women then clean, wash, and grind the grains until they are ready for cooking. These steps demonstrate the precision of traditional crop-processing methods and the practical knowledge residents have developed to make use of their environment's resources.
    Heritage festivals add a cultural and tourism dimension to Al-Khudeir season by introducing visitors to the stages of sorghum production and traditional preparation methods. Visitors can explore the tools used to process the grains and learn about customs associated with the harvest. These experiences enrich tourism and highlight aspects of rural life that have shaped the community and its relationship with the land.
    Al-Khudeir season remains a testament to the ability of Jazan's people to transform the bounty of their land into an enduring part of the region's collective memory. Beyond the harvest, it tells the story of a community that has preserved its cultural identity and drawn on the simplicity of everyday life to create a lasting heritage. This heritage contributes to Jazan's distinctive place in the Kingdom's cultural landscape.
    
    -- SPA
